system.name: FLARE
system.one_liner: a diagnostic framework that traces and diagnoses hang errors and performance regressions in thousand-plus-GPU LLM training clusters

components.name: Non-comm. Error
components.role: left scenario: a non-communication error where rank-0 halts at a different call stack than other ranks

components.name: Comm. Error
components.role: right scenario: a communication error where all ranks halt at the same communication call stack

components.name: Error GPU
components.role: the GPU/rank identified as the faulty source of a non-communication hang

components.name: Single-GPU operator
components.role: an operator executed independently on a single GPU in the call stack

components.name: Multi-GPU operator
components.role: an operator requiring coordination across multiple GPUs

components.name: Hang operator
components.role: the operator at which a rank's call stack is stuck/hung

components.name: Follow-up operator
components.role: operators that would execute after the hang point but do not run because the process is stuck

components.name: Rank=0
components.role: one training process rank whose call stack is shown

components.name: Rank=1
components.role: one training process rank whose call stack is shown

components.role: one training process rank whose call stack is shown

flows.what: rank-0 halts earlier at a non-communication function, distinct from other ranks
other ranks continue and stop at a communication-related function depending on rank-0
in the communication-error case, all ranks halt at the same communication function

content.key_idea: Comparing where each rank's call stack halts reveals non-communication hang errors (one rank stops earlier, at a different operator, than the rest), but communication hangs cannot be identified this way since all ranks stop at the same call stack.
content.reading_order: Left panel first (Non-comm. Error): compare rank-0's shorter, differently-terminated stack against Rank=1..N; then right panel (Comm. Error): all ranks terminate at the same hang operator; a legend on the right explains the four operator/box types.

palette.used_for: orange fill for single-GPU operator boxes
light teal fill for multi-GPU operator boxes
red diagonal hatch fill/outline marking the hang operator and the 'Error GPU' label

style.stroke: thin black strokes on boxes, red hatched fill for the hang operator, white fill for follow-up operators
style.font: Helvetica Neue and Helvetica Neue Bold sans-serif, very small (4pt)
style.arrows: vertical stack connectors per rank column, one curved red arrow pointing to the Error GPU rank

encoding.color_means: orange = single-GPU operator, teal = multi-GPU operator, red hatch = the hung operator (where a rank's stack is stuck), white = follow-up (not-yet-executed) operators
encoding.line_style_means: not applicable beyond fill/hatch coding; box position (height of stack) encodes how far each rank's call stack progressed before hanging
encoding.emphasis: the red hatched hang operator and the 'Error GPU' arrow in the left panel single out rank-0 as the fault source, while the right panel's uniform red row across all ranks visually shows why communication hangs are indistinguishable by this method alone
reusable_patterns: side-by-side per-rank call-stack columns compared to localize a fault
explicit legend decoding box color/fill as operator type/state
weaknesses: very small 4pt text reduces standalone legibility without the legend

evidence: Figure 5 illustrates an example of hang-error diagnosis via call stack analysis.
the training process of rank-0 crashes or is suspended due to a non-communication error, it halts at a call stack
the training processes of all ranks terminate at the same call stack of a communication function

summary: This figure compares two hang-error scenarios FLARE distinguishes via call-stack analysis. In the left panel (Non-communication Error), rank-0's call stack halts at a different, earlier operator than ranks 1..N, which continue until they reach a communication operator waiting on rank-0; the divergence lets FLARE flag rank-0's GPU as the error source. In the right panel (Communication Error), all ranks terminate at the identical communication-function call stack (e.g. allreduce/allgather), so this simple comparison cannot localize the fault, motivating the finer-grained intra-kernel inspection described elsewhere in the paper. A right-side legend decodes box colors: orange for single-GPU operators, teal for multi-GPU operators, red hatching for the hang operator, and white for follow-up operators not yet executed. The figure uses stacked per-rank columns of small boxes to make the comparison visually immediate.
summary_zh: 该图对比两种挂起错误场景：左侧非通信错误中，rank-0 的调用栈比其他 rank 更早停在不同算子处，从而被识别为故障源；右侧通信错误中，所有 rank 都停在同一个通信算子处，无法通过调用栈比较定位故障。图例说明单 GPU 算子、多 GPU 算子、挂起算子与后续算子四种方框含义。
